newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap 2.5 pct,seen resuming uptrend.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap 2.5 pct,seen resuming uptrend.

text.p: Istanbul shares jumped an average 2.51 percent in selective buying led by shares of largely state-owned firms on Thursday, resuming a medium-term uptrend after drifting sideways for two weeks, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 rose 2,041.29 points, or 2.51 percent to end at 83,505.37, compared to an all-time high of 83,772.33 on October 23. Trade volume was 17.39 trillion lira ($178.5 million), down from 19.27 trillion ($197.2 million) on Wednesday.
Brokers said selective buys flared in the second session after the index remained in a tight range in thin morning trade.
"Heavy buying began in shares of state companies and spilled over to other stocks. Activity in the state shares was based on privatisation expectations," said Hakan Demirbulak from Tatbank.
"The index seems to have turned upward from 81,500 support following a pull back," he added.

The index had surged 29.3 percent, hitting ten record closes from September 13 to October 23 in the medium-term uptrend which began with the breaching of 65,000 level. But it went into range-trading after failing to pierce 85,000 barrier last week.
